text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Wednesday morning newspapers:
- The governor of the Cypriot central bank said funds belonging to Slovenia which are deposited at the Cypriot branch of Yugoslav Beogradska Banka will remain frozen.

- Archeologists are digging out the remains of a Roman settlement near Maribor in eastern Slovenia. The large site on an area of about 20,000 square meters was discovered recently during motorway construction.
- Slovenian Hit Gorica lost 3-5 (0-5 first half) against Club Brugge from Belgium in the first leg of UEFA Cup second preliminary round on Tuesday.
- The new commercial televison station Pro Plus is expected to start operation from October, becoming the fourth commercial television in Slovenia.

- Marjan Podobnik, president of the conservative People's Party, said the first task for the government after the holidays would be to propose a new foreign minister after Zoran Thaler resigned last month.
- May average monthly gross wages increased to 143,169 ($835.8), a 1.2 percent increase from April and a 12 percent increase from the previous year.
- The number of tourists visiting the capital Ljubljana this summer jumped 40 percent from last year.
- Health resort Moravske Toplice is expected to be listed on the primary section of the Ljubljana bourse in September.
